question: Why Did WooCommerce Add a Number to My Product's URL Slug?
metaDescription: WordPress requires unique slugs sitewide — a matching page, post, or another product with the same slug forces a numbered suffix automatically.
shortAnswer: WordPress requires every published item's slug to be unique across the relevant scope, and when a new product's title generates a slug matching something that already exists — another product, a page, or even a post — WordPress automatically appends a number (like -2) to keep the URL unique, rather than allowing a genuine collision. This is expected, automatic conflict-avoidance, not a bug.

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

Slugs form the actual URL path, and WordPress can't have two different pieces of content resolving to the identical URL — when a new product's automatically generated slug (from its title) matches something that already exists anywhere relevant in the site's URL structure, WordPress resolves the conflict automatically by appending a number, ensuring the new item still gets a valid, working URL rather than failing to publish.

Common Causes

  • Two products with very similar or identical names, generating the same default slug from their titles.
  • A product name matching an existing page or post's slug, even if they're completely different types of content — slug uniqueness applies across content types in most default configurations.
  • A previously deleted (but not fully purged) product or page still holding a slug in the trash, which can sometimes still cause a conflict depending on how thoroughly it was removed.
  • Re-publishing a product after significant changes, if the system treats it as generating a new slug conflict against its own previous version in some edge cases.

How to Fix It

  1. Manually edit the product's slug to something distinct and more specific, rather than relying on the auto-generated, numbered version.
  2. Check whether the conflicting content (another page, post, or product) still needs its existing slug, or whether it could be adjusted instead if more appropriate.
  3. Set up a redirect if the numbered slug was already live and indexed, and you're now changing it to something cleaner.
